author: Jocelyn Flores
title: Loretto Academy welcomes 6 new scholars via Challenge Foundation - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores ,
1 hours ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — The Challenge Foundation awarded six young women with scholarships to Loretto Academy, totaling over $100,000.
The six incoming scholars; Mia Alvarez, Natalia Aguirre, Angie Martinez, Camila Ontiveros, Perlaruby Munoz and Valentine Martinez-Mendez, were selected through a competitive application process from elementary schools across El Paso.
Angie Martinez received her scholarship from the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. Mia Alvarez received her scholarship from the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. Natalia Aguirre received her scholarship from the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. Perlaruby Munoz received her scholarship from the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. Valentina Martinez Mendez received her scholarship from the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. The new scholars for the Challenge Foundation. Photo courtesy of the Challenge Foundation. Each student received a full-ride scholarship to attend Loretto Academy, beginning in sixth grade, along with individualized academic support, mentorship, college preparation and family services through graduation and beyond, according to the Challenge Foundation.
“This is so much more than a scholarship. Our program commits to young women`s lives for more than a decade,” Sylvia Hernandez, Co-director of TCF El Paso and a Loretto Academy alumna, said.
The ceremony featured remarks from the Challenge Foundation Board President Gene Myers and current UTEP student and Challenge alumna Karen Evangelista.
“Their support has been life-changing,” Evangelista said. “I have so much confidence now. I know where I’m going. And I know that if that would change, they’d still be there for me.”
Additionally, when each student received her scholarship, outgoing seniors from Loretto Academy personally welcomed the girls, “creating a visible bridge between the young women just beginning their journey and those preparing to enter college: a full-circle moments that underscores the program’s long-term commitment,” according to the Challenge Foundation.
The Challenge Foundation was founded in 2008 as a partnership with Loretto Academy and was established by Don and Janis McFall, with additional tuition support from the Richard G. Miller Foundation.
According to the foundation, Challenge scholars receive mentorship from trained community volunteers, participate in enrichment programming and experiential learning, and are supported through every stage of their academic and personal development.
The Challenge Foundation operates in Denver, Colorado, El Paso, Texas and Phoenix, Arizona.
